extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders, regulated entities, practitioners, and members of the public interested in Department of Labor proposed rules and notice-and-comment opportunities (e.g., employers, unions, benefits fiduciaries, attorneys, industry associations, state agencies, and potential commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: A machine-readable listing (Federal Register API JSON) of Department of Labor proposed rules and related notices (abstracts, metadata, links) intended to inform stakeholders and solicit public comments. The page summarizes multiple NPRMs, extensions of comment periods, and sub-regulatory guidance across DOL components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Employer Status under the FLSA/FMLA/MSPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes to clarify how to determine joint employer status under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) in Part 791 and to amend FMLA and MSPA provisions to determine joint employer status using the Department's FLSA analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to provide clarity and uniformity for workers, employers, and enforcement personnel by offering a nationwide standard for investigators and law enforcement; aims to marshal commonality between judicial approaches close to statutory construction to simplify enforcement, reduce litigation, and provide a reliable uniform analysis. (See document_number 2026-07959.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Walking-Working Surfaces — fixed ladder fall-protection requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes removing a deadline that required all fixed ladders extending more than 24 feet above a lower level to be equipped with personal fall arrest systems or ladder safety systems, and seeks comment on repealing or revising the requirement that employers use personal fall arrest systems on all fixed ladders over 24 feet tall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA is considering permitting employers to continue to use ladder cages or wells instead of personal fall arrest systems; solicits stakeholder comment on repeal/revision and effects on safety and compliance. (See document_number 2026-06578.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiduciary Duty Prudence Safe Harbor for Selecting Designated Investment Alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes a regulation that clarifies and provides a safe harbor for a fiduciary's duty of prudence under ERISA when selecting designated investment alternatives for participant-directed individual account plans, including asset allocation funds with alternative assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implements statutory/Executive Order direction (section 3(c) of E.O. 14330) and is aimed at fiduciaries of 401(k)-style plans; the proposal defines criteria and safe-harbor conditions for prudence in selecting options. (See document_number 2026-06178.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevailing Wage Computation for Certain Foreign National Employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes revisions to ETA regulations governing prevailing wage computation under PERM and LCAs (H-1B, H-1B1, E-3 and EB-2/EB-3), including changes to the Department's four-tiered prevailing wage structure based on the OEWS wage survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to better align prevailing wage levels with wages paid to U.S. workers in the occupation/area, strengthen program integrity to reduce incentives to replace U.S. workers, and more effectively prevent adverse effects on wages and working conditions of U.S. workers. (See document_number 2026-06017.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmacy Benefit Manager (PBM) Fee Disclosure Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes to require PBMs and affiliated brokerage/consulting providers to disclose information about their compensation to fiduciaries of self-insured group health plans subject to ERISA for purposes of ERISA's prohibited transaction exemption for services arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures are intended to enable fiduciaries to assess the reasonableness of service arrangements and compensation; the listing also includes an extension of the comment period to allow consideration of statutory changes from the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026. (See document_numbers 2026-01907 and 2026-04084.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee vs. Independent Contractor Status Analysis (FLSA/FMLA/MSPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes rescinding the existing analysis in 29 CFR part 795 and replacing it with the Department's 2021 analysis (with modifications), and applying that analysis to FMLA and MSPA which incorporate FLSA employment definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This would standardize the tests used across statutes administered by the Department and affect classification outcomes for workers and employers; comments may address the proposed analytical framework and its application. (See document_number 2026-03962.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in Coverage — machine-readable file content and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments to PHSA/ERISA/IRC regulations to improve standardization, accuracy, and accessibility of public pricing disclosures for non-grandfathered group health plans and issuers, including adding contextual files and data elements (product type, network name, enrollment counts), changing aggregation/reporting levels, removing unlikely provider-to-service mappings, increasing reporting period, lowering claims threshold for out-of-network historical data, and reducing reporting cadence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also proposes improved findability (text file and footer with URLs/contact info), requiring online/paper pricing info to be available by phone, and treating satisfaction of this requirement as satisfying section 114 of the No Surprises Act; aims at clearer machine-readable outputs for consumers and regulators. (See document_numbers 2025-23693 and 2025-23693 (related entries).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to Electronic Disclosure Safe Harbors — Paper Benefit Statement Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes narrow amendments to two electronic disclosure safe harbors implementing SECURE 2.0 section 338 to require retirement plans to provide paper benefit statements in certain cases and to update the Department's electronic disclosure safe harbors accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two existing safe harbors permit broad electronic disclosure under prescribed conditions; the amendments implement a Congressional mandate and clarify when paper statements must be furnished. (See document_number 2026-03723.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Insurance Carrier Security Deposit Requirements (Longshore & Harbor Workers' Compensation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sub-regulatory guidance establishing a rubric for adjusting authorized insurance carriers' collateral/security deposit obligations under the LHWCA based on fiscal stability and performance within the Longshore industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to provide predictability for carriers' capital planning, avoid arbitrary adjustments, standardize compliance across the industry, and ensure carriers secure liabilities; clarifies securitization requirements but does not supersede existing regulations. (See document_number 2026-02537.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat Injury and Illness Prevention Standard (OSHA) — post-hearing comment procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed OSHA standard for Heat Injury and Illness Prevention in Outdoor and Indoor Work Settings; the agency held an informal public hearing and extended the period to submit post-hearing comments to allow additional evidence, data, written responses to hearing questions, and final briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The extension facilitates submission of post-hearing evidence and arguments by those who timely filed Notices of Intention to Appear; commenters may submit data and responses relevant to proceedings. (See document_number 2025-18670.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of Comment Periods for Major NPRMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple notices extend comment periods for pending NPRMs (e.g., Transparency in Coverage; various OSHA chemical/caricinogen rulemakings; VEVRAA/Section 503/EO 11246 rescission), often to allow stakeholders more time to review proposals and submit data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These extension notices advise whether prior commenters need to resubmit, set new deadlines, and sometimes explain statutory developments prompting the extension; they are procedural but affect stakeholders' opportunity to participate. (See multiple document_numbers such as 2026-04084, 2025-16921, 2025-16919, 2025-16920, 2025-15898, 2025-15900, 2025-15899, 2025-15902.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications to Regulations Implementing VEVRAA (notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and NPRM to revise DOL regulations implementing the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974; includes extension of comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters are encouraged to file by the extended date; DOL will consider comments received through the close of the extended period. (See document_number 2025-16921.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission of EO 11246 Implementing Regulations (notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: NPRM proposing to rescind the Department of Labor's implementing regulations for Executive Order 11246, as amended; includes extension of comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice explains deadlines and how previously submitted comments will be handled; opportunity for stakeholders to address rescission impacts. (See document_number 2025-16919.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications to Regulations Implementing Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act (notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: NPRM to revise implementing regulations for Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act, as amended; includes extension of comment period and instructions for commenters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar procedural guidance on submission and consideration of comments; intended to solicit stakeholder input on regulatory revisions. (See document_number 2025-16920.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal-State Unemployment Compensation (UC) Program — data availability to Federal officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes to require disclosure of confidential UC information to Federal officials, including DOL-OIG, for UC program oversight and audits to ensure proper oversight and to identify and address fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects state-federal data sharing; balances confidentiality with oversight needs; commenters may address privacy, statutory authority, and implementation mechanisms. (See document_number 2025-16645.)

rubrics_metrics.name: OSHA Chemical/Carcinogen NPRMs — extended comment periods (13 Carcinogens, Acrylonitrile, 1,3-Butadiene, Benzene)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices extending comment periods by 60 days for OSHA NPRMs on 13 carcinogens (including 4-nitrobiphenyl), Acrylonitrile, 1,3-Butadiene, and Benzene to allow stakeholders additional time to review and collect information/data necessary for comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions support stakeholder ability to prepare substantive comments and data; procedural but materially affects participation timelines. (See document_numbers 2025-15898, 2025-15900, 2025-15899, 2025-15902.)
